summary.text: Jim Pillen is the Republican governor of Nebraska, seeking a second term. A veterinarian and livestock producer who chairs Pillen Family Farms, he served on the University of Nebraska Board of Regents before winning the governorship in 2022 with 59.2% of the vote. His administration has pursued property-tax changes, and in 2023 he signed LB 574, which sets a 12-week abortion limit and also restricts gender-altering procedures for people under 19.

paragraphs.text: Pillen grew up on a farm in Platte County, Nebraska, where he raised pigs with his father, Dale, and graduated from Lakeview High School.

He earned a bachelor's degree in animal science from the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, where he played defensive back for the Cornhuskers football team from 1975 to 1978, and a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine from Kansas State University.
Pillen returned to Nebraska in 1983 and opened a small animal practice and a swine consulting practice.
He started Pillen Family Farms in 1993 and added DNA Genetics in 2003, and he remains a practicing veterinarian and chair of the family business, which his children later joined.
He also served as president of the Columbus Area Chamber of Commerce and chaired the Columbus Community Hospital Board of Directors.
Pillen served on the University of Nebraska Board of Regents from 2013 to 2023, and was chair in 2020.
He won the 2022 Republican primary for governor and defeated Democrat Carol Blood in the general election, taking office on January 5, 2023, as Nebraska's 41st governor.
Pillen and his wife, Suzanne, have four children and eight grandchildren.
